speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of your rash, specifically noting if there are any honey-colored crusts or a "stuck-on" waxy look? Have you noticed any pain, itching, or recent sun exposure in the affected areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap) with possible atopic diathesis.

While the family history of psoriasis is noted, the clinical picture of a red, scaly rash in a 3-month-old that worsens with cold weather is most consistent with seborrheic dermatitis. I will monitor the condition; if the rash persists or spreads, we may consider a trial of mild topical steroids, but currently, gentle cleansing and emollients are the primary treatment.
